claims.text: Gd5Si2Ge2 is a known magnetocaloric material.
Targeted thermomechanical processing of Gd5Si2Ge2 can enhance its magnetocaloric properties.
Conventionally processed Gd5Si2Ge2 has a relatively broad magnetic phase transition.
Conventionally processed Gd5Si2Ge2 has relatively high hysteresis.
Heterogeneity in grain size and phase distribution causes the broad transition and higher hysteresis of the baseline alloy.
Controlled annealing, severe plastic deformation, or high-pressure high-temperature treatment can produce a finer-grained and more phase-homogeneous Gd5Si2Ge2 microstructure.
The relevant operating temperature for this material is often near room temperature.
The proposed processing route will reduce grain size, improve phase homogeneity, and reduce internal stresses.
A more uniform, finer-grained, and lower-stress microstructure sharpens the magnetic phase transition.
A more uniform, finer-grained, and lower-stress microstructure minimizes magnetic hysteresis.
Microstructural refinement improves alignment of magnetic moments at grain boundaries and interfaces.
Improved alignment of magnetic moments at boundaries and interfaces concentrates the magnetic entropy change during the phase transition.
Improved alignment of magnetic moments reduces hysteretic energy losses.
The processed material will exhibit a larger magnetic entropy change than conventionally processed Gd5Si2Ge2.
The processed material will exhibit less magnetic hysteresis than conventionally processed Gd5Si2Ge2.
The achievable benefit from microstructural refinement is limited by the alloy's intrinsic properties.
Insufficient refinement or degradation of phase purity can prevent improvement in magnetocaloric response.
The magnitude of entropy-change enhancement and hysteresis reduction depends on processing parameters and the degree of microstructural refinement.
